summary: 001C leakage scanners do not sufficiently prove fail-ability on real artifact and candidate surfaces because the canonical gate scans sanitized projections or constants and uses decoupled synthetic positive controls.
contract_basis: COMPUTED-EVIDENCE-PROVENANCE-CONTRACT-001A requires computed, fail-able provenance-backed evidence rather than unconditional clean reports or static dictionaries.

critical_failure_modes.description: Candidate inputs and trace rows are reduced before scanning, so forbidden fields inserted into full real objects are not part of the canonical scanned surface.
The positive control is the same synthetic object for each scanner and is not injected into a copy of the corresponding real surface.
Artifact path scanning uses a constant object instead of scanning actual artifact filenames and paths.
Metric provenance rows are not represented as a required leakage scanner surface.
Leakage metric provenance records broad input artifact paths and output row IDs, but not actual consumed surface IDs for sanitized scanner inputs.
Serialized-state provenance records forbidden_source_scan_result as clean=true and hits=[] constants.
Existing leakage tests assert current pass conditions but do not inject forbidden fields into copies of real surfaces and require failure.

falsification_condition: The blocker would be falsified by committed evidence showing full real candidate, trace, observation, artifact inventory, and metric provenance surfaces scanned, with positive controls injected into copies of those same surfaces and failure-path tests proving detection.
insufficient_evidence: Synthetic positive-control detection on a separate object.
Clean real scans over sanitized projections.
Broad input artifact hashes without consumed scanner surface IDs.
Unconditional clean fields in provenance rows.
resulting_action: Suspend 001C as downstream positive evidence until a bounded leakage-gate repair and rerun exists.
